findings.title: docs/configuration.md: three rows contradict the code (legionella interval 7 vs 10 days; 60 s echo grace not applied)
findings.claim: docs/configuration.md holds 3 ledger rows whose executed check contradicts production: two settings-table rows give the anti-legionella interval default as 7 days while every _OPTION_FIELDS row and ThermalParameters default to 10, and line 894's sentence says readings in the first 60 s after a write are not counted while pump_arbiter.hold counts a differing reading at +5 s (and ECHO_GRACE_S is 20 s).
findings.mechanism: The table cell and the prose were written against a default and a grace the code does not carry: DEFAULT_DHW_LEGIONELLA_INTERVAL_DAYS is 10.0 (config_flow _OPTION_FIELDS hot_water row, thermal_model.ThermalParameters), and hold() drops the write record (counts a miss) on the first differing reading with no time gate, so no window of 60 s (or 20 s) is honoured.

leads.what: On the export, the closed-loop learner at plant_error 1.35 (4.25 kW pump, 3 days) drives the heat-loss scale from 1.000 to 0.300, away from the truth, and the comfort breach rises from 0.00 to 5.42 K·h. With a correct model it stays at 0.979. tests/rolling.py's 'moves towards the real error' check would fail. Command: claims.py, CLAIM learner_converges_35pct.

hold() counts a differing reading as a miss at +5 s after a write (the write record is dropped), with no echo-grace gate. ECHO_GRACE_S (20 s) is applied only in _edited. A Tuya echo inside the 8 s sent-value window would read as 'the pump does not hold'. Seen after the baseline diff (see exposure); measured by claims.py echo_grace_60s.

In this export tests/doc_claims.py crashes on the non-UTF-8 AppleDouble docs/._configuration.md, which is an export artefact. On a clean copy it fails in tests/plan_view.py: 'space slot energy 46.595 kWh != schedule 46.621 kWh'. So the registered doc claims could not be read from it this round.
